business_scope: Mathematical count of a bounded, static IM fan-out snapshot; no network actions or upstream performance claims
prerequisites: 01.01–01.03 first-pass scalar values, conditions, loops, ordinary functions
01.04 arrays, slices, range, len and empty input
first_pass: Discrete objects, sets, distinct elements, empty set, order versus membership
Relations as ordered pairs with explicit completeness assumptions
Finite sums, pair counts, powers, logarithmic halving and rounding
Input dimensions n/m/D/B/Q; basic-operation cost model versus elapsed time
O upper bound, Omega lower bound, Theta tight bound with fixed constants and thresholds
Bounded scalar/slice counting function with validity flag and overflow-safe limits
second_pass: Worst case over fixed-size input domain
Average linear scan only under stated location/absence distribution
Amortized insertion under an explicitly hypothetical doubling-capacity model
Finite probability space, events, random variables, expectation and linearity without independence
Conditional probability and when event probabilities may be multiplied
Induction, loop invariants, termination and validated arithmetic preconditions

canonical_fanout_model.m: distinct receiver-user entries after excluding sender
canonical_fanout_model.d_i: online device count for receiver i
canonical_fanout_model.Q: n*D initial tasks only for the same target snapshot
canonical_fanout_model.sender: all sender devices excluded in baseline; optional sender synchronization explicitly changes model
canonical_fanout_model.attempts: A=Q+R when each initial task gets its first attempt, R=total actual extra attempts
canonical_fanout_model.batches: ceil(Q/b) is minimum packing count under free grouping; retry time dependencies can increase actual batches

counter_contract.scope: counts only; neither creates task records nor sends messages

boundaries: ceil(log2 n) only for upward-halving model to <=1; n=0 separately defined
m remains receiver-user entry count, never silently redefined as device count
Only a task upper limit yields O bound, not automatically Theta
Zero inner dimension can leave n outer-loop operations
Teaching function hard bounds are distinct from unbounded abstract asymptotic model
Observed ratio does not prove future probability or frequency convergence
At-most-one retry differs from actually executing an extra attempt
Amortized constant does not imply single-operation worst-case constant or Go growth factor guarantee
not_yet_prerequisites: production online snapshot or queue implementation
probability limit theorems or unbounded retry models
upstream_inspection: No new OpenIM implementation facts asserted in this chapter. IM models are original teaching assumptions.
validation: Static review and document checks only; no curriculum code execution, tests, build or deployment.
